_comment: Shared cross-language pin for STEP schema-conversion attribute reconciliation: padding the attributes a newer schema APPENDED (#1416) and trimming the ones the target lacks, in both directions (#7683). Both halves run their own converter over every case: rust/export/tests/schema_upconvert_parity.rs and packages/export/src/schema-upconvert-sweep.parity.test.ts. Which rows must exist is gated by rust/export/src/schema_registry_tests.rs (sweep_fixture_names_every_trimmed_and_padded_type_7683), which re-derives every (from, to, type) the converter trims or pads from core's EXPRESS registry: the types whose attribute NAME list is a strict prefix of the other schema's. The rows appended for #7683 use the input 'a0','a1',... so a trimmed or padded slot is visible by position; the rows before them were derived from packages/data's generated tables and use $. Hand-written vectors and negative controls carry their reason in `why`. Exception: the two IFC4 -> IFC4X3 IFCCARTESIANPOINTLIST* rows (#5755) come from the IFC4 EXPRESS, because packages/data's IFC4 table wrongly lists TagList for IFC4. The rows appended for #7739 pin the types of schema_positional_renames.json (attributes a schema renamed in place) the same way. DO NOT hand-edit a row to make a test pass.

cases.why: mid-list insertion must NOT be padded
an attribute-less line is not fabricated into one attribute
a comma inside a string is not an attribute separator
a comma inside a nested list is not an attribute separator
a renamed type is padded to its TARGET type count
